Salesforce CRM and Data Cloud

Source: vignettes/salesforce.Rmd
salesforce.Rmd

Salesforce CRM stores records such as accounts and contacts in objects, which you can query with Salesforce’s query language, SOQL. Data Cloud provides a separate SQL query API. shinyOAuthDB lets a Shiny app use either source with the signed-in visitor’s Salesforce permissions.

Use oauth_db_salesforce_api() for CRM objects and oauth_db_salesforce_data_cloud_api() for Data Cloud. Both return data frames or native API results and can share one Salesforce sign-in. The example lets the visitor choose which source to query.

Register the Shiny app

Create an External Client App in Salesforce Setup. Salesforce recommends these for new integrations; existing Connected Apps can still be used. Enable the authorization-code flow, PKCE, and the following OAuth scopes:

Scope Purpose
openid and profile Identify the visitor through OpenID Connect
api Query Salesforce APIs with the visitor’s permissions
refresh_token Renew access without another browser sign-in
cdp_query_api Run Data Cloud SQL; omit for a CRM-only app

Register the exact callback URI used by Shiny, for example http://localhost:8100. For a hosted app, use its HTTPS URL. Configure the client-secret requirement to match your registration and deployment. The example uses a confidential server app with a client secret.

Enable Issue JSON Web Token (JWT)-based access tokens for named users in the app’s OAuth security settings. This token format works with shinyOAuth’s validation and the APIs used here. See Salesforce’s JWT access-token configuration.

Users need API access and permission to use the client app. CRM object, field and record access still comes from Salesforce. Data Cloud also needs the relevant license, query permissions, and access to the chosen data space. Requesting an OAuth scope does not grant those permissions.

See Salesforce’s OAuth registration guide and OAuth scope definitions.

Collect the settings

Save your settings in .Renviron and restart R:

OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-consumer-key
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-consumer-secret
OAUTHDB_SALESFORCE_LOGIN_URL=https://example.my.salesforce.com
OAUTHDB_SALESFORCE_INSTANCE_URL=https://example.my.salesforce.com

Replace example with your Salesforce My Domain. LOGIN_URL is the authorization server. It can also be https://login.salesforce.com, or https://test.salesforce.com for a sandbox. INSTANCE_URL is the trusted Salesforce org origin for API calls, without a path. Use the org’s My Domain API URL rather than its Lightning UI URL. A login origin and an API origin can differ.

A complete app

The app queries when the visitor clicks Run query. Replace the Data Cloud object and field names with ones available in your data space.

Install mirai for background OAuth and data fetching. Each query task keeps the app responsive while Salesforce runs and returns its results.

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

client <- oauth_db_salesforce_client(
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  login_url = Sys.getenv(
    "OAUTHDB_SALESFORCE_LOGIN_URL",
    "https://login.salesforce.com"
  ),
  data_cloud = TRUE
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),

    selectInput("source", "Query source", c("CRM", "Data Cloud")),

    actionButton("query", "Run query"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),

  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server(
    "auth",
    client,
    auto_redirect = FALSE,
    async = TRUE
  )

  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  instance_url <- Sys.getenv(
    "OAUTHDB_SALESFORCE_INSTANCE_URL",
    "https://example.my.salesforce.com"
  )

  crm <- oauth_db_salesforce_api(auth$connection, instance_url)
  cloud <- oauth_db_salesforce_data_cloud_api(auth$connection, instance_url)

  tasks <- list(CRM = oauth_db_task(crm), `Data Cloud` = oauth_db_task(cloud))

  observeEvent(input$query, {
    selected <- req(tasks[[req(input$source)]])

    statement <- if (input$source == "CRM") {
      "SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 20"
    } else {
      "SELECT ssot__Id__c FROM ssot__Individual__dlm LIMIT 20"
    }

    selected$invoke(statement)
  })

  output$rows <- renderTable({
    selected <- req(tasks[[req(input$source)]])

    selected$result()
  })
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*", onStart = function() {
    mirai::daemons(2)

    onStop(function() mirai::daemons(0))
  }),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

Open http://localhost:8100 in a regular browser. Embedded IDE viewers cannot complete OAuth redirects. For CRM only, set data_cloud = FALSE and omit the Data Cloud helper and query choice.

The app hides saved results after sign-out, account replacement or loss of required scopes. See Getting started when adding other result caches.

Query CRM objects

$query() follows query locators until all result pages have been fetched. include_deleted = TRUE uses QueryAll, which can include deleted and archived records under Salesforce’s permissions and retention rules.

crm$query("SELECT Id, Name, Parent.Name FROM Account LIMIT 20")
crm$query("SELECT Id, IsDeleted FROM Account LIMIT 20", include_deleted = TRUE)
crm$objects()
crm$describe("Account")

count <- crm$query("SELECT COUNT() FROM Account", raw = TRUE)

count$totalSize

Queries return data frames, with relationships and child-query results in list columns. Use $describe() for field definitions, or raw = TRUE for the native records and metadata. Large integers stay as strings; ordinary JSON numbers become R numeric values.

SOQL is supplied as written. The helper does not interpolate parameters, create DBI connections, or implement CRM record mutations. See Salesforce’s Query resource and Query More Results.

Query Data Cloud with bound parameters

The Data Cloud client uses Query Connect API, which accepts the same Salesforce sign-in as CRM. You can select a data space when creating it.

Specify a data space with dataspace = "reporting" when creating the client. api_version can select another supported version, at least 64.0.

cloud$query(
  "SELECT ssot__Id__c FROM ssot__Individual__dlm WHERE CreatedDate__c >= :since LIMIT 20",
  parameters = list(
    list(name = "since", type = "date", value = "2026-01-01")
  )
)

Each parameter has name, type, and value strings, using the SQL types accepted by Salesforce. Values are bound separately from SQL. Duplicate names and incomplete descriptors are rejected locally.

BIGINT and NUMERIC columns stay as strings to preserve precision. Dates and times also stay as strings; nested values use list columns. See ?oauth_db_salesforce_data_cloud_api for other result conversions and raw metadata.

The client submits once, polls the query ID and fetches remaining rows with offsets. See the Query API overview and Query Connect example.

Token renewal and query lifetime

Each client uses the current token for the visitor’s Shiny session and discards results after sign-out or account changes. Read requests can refresh and retry once after HTTP 401. SQL submission doesn’t retry automatically; check Salesforce after a submission failure before running the query again.

timeout covers submission and result fetching. Results must fit in R memory. A timeout or sign-out doesn’t cancel a submitted Data Cloud query, so limit result sizes in SQL.

Salesforce can omit the token’s expiry time. shinyOAuth then warns and uses its configured fallback lifetime. See its shinyOAuth.default_expires_in option if you need to match a deployment’s session policy, and the client function help for token and request options.
